Lessons.Title: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 3)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: construct a quadratic revenue function from price and demand, interpret the zeros and maximum in context, and choose a reasonable domain. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L07 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/7/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/7/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source transitions from projectile motion to price/revenue modeling.

Original hypothetical ticket market: estimated tickets sold at price p dollars is q(p)=60−2p for 0≤p≤30. Revenue is price times quantity R(p)=p(60−2p)=60p−2p² dollars. For continuous price approximation, the graph is downward-opening with zeros p0 and p30; in real ticket sales counts must be nonnegative integers and prices may be restricted to cents or whole dollars.

Complete square R(p)=450−2(p−15)², showing maximum revenue $450 at price$15 and expected30 tickets. At price$10 and price$20, revenue is $400 in each case, reflecting symmetry around the maximizing price. Negative prices or quantities are outside the model and cannot be treated as feasible points.

Student task: create a table for prices0,5,10,15,20,25,30, draw a graph with common axes, interpret R=0 at both endpoints in different ways and critique whether real demand actually obeys a linear rule. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for model from context, verified vertex/zeros, domain and critique of assumptions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Revenue maximum
KeyConcepts.Definition: The vertex of a downward quadratic maximizes the continuous model.

KeyConcepts.Title: Contextual zeros
KeyConcepts.Definition: A zero can correspond to free price or zero demand, with different meanings.
KeyConcepts.Example: p0 price zero; p30 demand zero.

WorkedExamples.Title: Form revenue polynomial
WorkedExamples.Question: If q=60−2p, find R(p).
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the independently authored model, derive each step and check against original data.
Steps: Revenue equals price times ticket count.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find maximizing price
WorkedExamples.Question: What p maximizes R?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the independently authored model, derive each step and check against original data.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find and interpret zero revenue
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve p(60−2p)=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the independently authored model, derive each step and check against original data.
Steps: At p0 tickets may be numerous but price is free.
At p30 demand model predicts0 tickets.
Both yield zero revenue for different reasons.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using quantity q as though it were revenue

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: At p>30 model predicts negative tickets.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming hypothetical revenue maximizer is real market optimization

SummaryPoints: Revenue from linear demand is often a downward-opening quadratic.
Zeros p0 and p30 have distinct contextual meanings.
Teacher reviews economic assumptions and graph interpretations.
